chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Suleiman ibn Salim, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: When you stipulate the conditions of Mut'ah upon the woman, and she accepts it and makes the marriage binding, then return to her your first condition after the marriage. If she approves it, then it is approved; and if she does not approve it, then what was from the condition before the marriage is not binding upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on modifying or re-asserting marriage conditions in Mut'ah after the contract is formed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the dynamic nature of contractual stipulations in temporary marriage (Mut'ah), emphasizing that initial conditions are not irrevocably binding until confirmed by mutual consent post-nikah. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'ijbar' (binding agreement) through continued consent, ensuring that both parties retain agency to validate or nullify terms as the marital bond is formalized. This mechanism safeguards against unilateral imposition of terms, reflecting the broader Islamic legal emphasis on mutual agreement (taradi) in contracts.
